finding_responses.response: Verified per owner decision (a). Cancellation is now observed on the resident path at both boundaries: pre-dispatch (state.shutdown.is_cancelled() || reply.is_closed() at src/backend.rs:134, mirroring the CLI supervisor's pre-spawn check) and in-flight (dispatch_with_cancellation's select! on reply.closed()/state.shutdown.cancelled() firing a CancellationToken that is handed through the manager lease to the leased worker). The worker runs the existing design section 5 sequence - cooperative cancel frame for the active request, bounded CANCELLATION_GRACE, terminate_preserving with process-tree reaping - and reports the CLI-shaped 200/exit_code:-1 interruption (WORKER_TERMINATION_FAILURE instead of false success if containment fails). Deterministic test resident_backend_client_cancellation_retires_the_active_worker (tests/resident_backend.rs:199) uses the new request-slow fixture with a dropped handler and asserts retirement, permit release, and temp-dir reclamation; ran 3x, green each time. The two round-1 consequences (request pinned to its full deadline; unreachable pre-dispatch branch) are both eliminated.

Verified per owner decision (2). tests/backend_contract.rs adds the three design section 9 comparisons over one shared fixture (contract_echo.py, with the contract_runtime/yt_dlp stand-in shelling out to the same script so both backends run literally the same arguments): success is a byte-identical RunResponse on both backends; timeout diverges exactly as approved (CLI 200/exit_code:-1 vs resident 500/WORKER_TIMEOUT with retirement asserted); business errors keep the identical shape for unstructured failures while the resident-only structured channel surfaces 500 plus the verbatim worker code. The test file and each divergence test reference review/owner-decisions.md, making the approved API change traceable from code. No behavior was changed - the diff only records and tests the existing shapes.
